name: qdrant-vertical-scaling
prompt: We're running ~60M 768-dim vectors on a single self-hosted node and RAM usage hovers around 85%, with latency starting to wobble. We'd rather not move to a distributed cluster yet. How much memory should this realistically need, and what's the right way to size the box up?

rubric.text: Endorses scaling up vertically (more RAM) since they're at the ~80% threshold and want to avoid distribution
Estimates RAM per component for 60M x 768-d (vectors, HNSW index, ID tracker, payload indexes) for the structures kept in RAM, rather than a single blended multiplier
Recommends reserving ~20% headroom above the working set for optimizer/OS cache

Offers quantization to cut the RAM requirement, noting that the quantized copy (1/4 the size for scalar, 1/32 for binary) is stored alongside the originals and RAM only drops when the original vectors move to disk
Notes ~100M vectors/node as the rough single-node ceiling (the user still has runway)
If on Cloud, ensure replication_factor >=2 so the resize rolling-restart is zero-downtime
Pushes horizontal scaling / sharding despite being within single-node limits and wanting to avoid it
Treats the 80% RAM threshold as a soft/gradual limit rather than a performance cliff
